about_blocks.text: About the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being
about_blocks.html: About the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being

about_blocks.text: The Centre for Wholeness & Well Being is an outpatient counselling and recovery centre in Calgary's Currie neighbourhood, in the city's southwest. It is not a residential rehab. People come in for appointments and go home afterwards, and the centre says plainly that it does not offer medically supervised withdrawal or 24-hour care. It works out of Brad House, a heritage building at 3911 Trasimene Crescent SW, and is run by a registered charity, the Alberta Association for Better Communities.
about_blocks.html: The Centre for Wholeness & Well Being is an outpatient counselling and recovery centre in Calgary's Currie neighbourhood, in the city's southwest. It is not a residential rehab. People come in for appointments and go home afterwards, and the centre says plainly that it does not offer medically supervised withdrawal or 24-hour care. It works out of Brad House, a heritage building at 3911 Trasimene Crescent SW, and is run by a registered charity, the Alberta Association for Better Communities.

about_blocks.text: Its addiction program is called Empower Recovery. The centre describes it as a non-12-step, non-residential pathway that mixes counselling, recovery coaching and family support, so people can keep working and stay at home while they get help with substance use. It is aimed at people who need more structure than an occasional counselling session, people who have just finished residential treatment, and people who have returned to use and want support quickly. The centre says there is no waitlist for clients it considers a good fit.

about_blocks.text: Plenty of clients come for reasons other than substance use. The centre also sees people for anxiety, burnout, grief, trauma and stress, and for life changes such as postpartum, perimenopause and caregiving. Families can get help too. Its Pathways to Reconnection service prepares relatives to invite a loved one into care without confrontation, and Pathways to Wholeness offers continuing care after a program or treatment stay ends. The centre also offers one-to-one psychedelic integration coaching for people who have had, or are considering, a psychedelic experience. It describes this as harm reduction and states that it does not provide substances.

about_blocks.text: The centre also uses two devices it calls EXOMind and EMVital. On its website it describes EXOMind as non-invasive, Health Canada-cleared neurostimulation based on TMS, and says it is used alongside counselling, not on its own. Other services on site include acupuncture, massage therapy, Reiki, a Neuro Rebalancing sound program and a salt room called the Siwa Sanctuary. Google reviewers also mention sound baths and women's circles among its events.

about_blocks.text: Co-founders Ryan Snow and Sue Snow lead the counselling work. Ryan is a certified addiction counsellor, recovery coach and ARISE-trained interventionist who writes openly about his own recovery, and Sue holds an M.Ed. and counselling credentials including MPCC. Fees are not published. The first consultation is free, the centre issues receipts for health benefit claims, and financing is available through Beautifi for services over $1,000.

centre.faq_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Centre for Wholeness & Well Being

faqs.question: Is the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being a residential rehab?

answer_blocks.text: No. It is an outpatient counselling and recovery centre in southwest Calgary, and clients go home after each appointment. There are no beds, no detox and no 24-hour care. The centre says that if someone needs medically supervised withdrawal, a safer place to stay or psychiatric stabilization, residential or hospital care is the better fit, and it will tell you so.

The centre says that if someone needs medically supervised withdrawal, a safer place to stay or psychiatric stabilization, residential or hospital care is the better fit, and it will tell you so.

faqs.question: What is the Empower Recovery program?

answer_blocks.text: Empower Recovery is the centre's non-residential, non-12-step recovery program for people dealing with substance use. It combines counselling, recovery coaching and family support, with EXOMind sessions added when the team thinks they are appropriate. It suits people who want more structure than occasional counselling but cannot step away from work or family, and people stepping down from a residential program.

faqs.question: How much does it cost, and can I use my benefits?

answer_blocks.text: The centre does not publish its fees. It says pricing for counselling and coaching is flexible and is discussed during a free first consultation. Receipts are provided so you can claim through a health benefits plan, and its recovery.com profile lists plans including Manulife, Sun Life, Medavie Blue Cross, Green Shield, Empire Life and Industrial Alliance. Monthly financing through Beautifi is available for services over $1,000.

faqs.question: What is EXOMind, and how does the centre use it?

answer_blocks.text: EXOMind is a neurostimulation device that the centre describes as non-invasive, Health Canada-cleared and based on TMS (transcranial magnetic stimulation). The centre says it uses EXOMind as one part of a care plan alongside counselling and recovery support, not as a stand-alone treatment, and that a course is often about six sessions, though plans vary. Ask at your consultation whether it suits you.

faqs.question: Can families get help if a loved one is not ready?

answer_blocks.text: Yes. The centre's Pathways to Reconnection service helps families prepare for a difficult conversation and invite a loved one into care without pressure or confrontation. Family members can also book counselling for themselves, and family involvement is built into the Empower Recovery program when it helps.

faqs.question: Who runs the Centre for Wholeness & Well Being?

answer_blocks.text: It was co-founded by Ryan Snow and Sue Snow, who are both counsellors there. Ryan is a certified addiction counsellor, recovery coach and ARISE-trained interventionist, and Sue holds a B.A. and M.Ed. with credentials including CCDC and MPCC. The centre is operated by the Alberta Association for Better Communities, a registered charity.

faqs.question: Where is the centre and how do I get there?

answer_blocks.text: The centre is in Brad House at 3911 Trasimene Crescent SW in Currie, Calgary (T3E 7J6), about 10 to 15 minutes by car from downtown. Google Maps lists the street as Trasimeno Crescent, but it is the same place. The centre suggests driving north on Quesnay Wood Drive SW, turning left on Normandy Drive, left on Alexandria and then left onto Trasimene. Parking is on site.
